# Orkas

**An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.**

Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the **Commander** what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent** — to work on it together.

Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A **project** holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. **To-dos** split the work between people and agents, **Auto-advance** lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and **scheduled automations** repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business.

**[⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## What the team delivers

- **Videos, voice-overs and images** — VideoStudio, VoiceStudio, ImageStudio
- **Research reports, SEO audits and market analysis** — DeepResearcher, SeoGeoAgent, StockAnalyser
- **Posts, articles, newsletters and slide decks** — ContentWriter, PptMaker
- **Websites, UI and code** — UIDesigner, ProductDeveloper
- **Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files** — OfficeWorker
- **E-commerce work** — product research, listings, review analysis, sales analysis and catalog changes, from five e-commerce agents
- **Complex work that takes several agents** — the Commander splits it up, hands each part to the right agent and combines the results; for example, market research that becomes a report, a slide deck and a launch video

16 specialists ship with the app, each with its own skills, memory and tools. Browse 30+ agents in the [agent marketplace](https://orkas.ai/views/marketplace/gs/agents/?source=gh-orkas), or describe the role you need and the Commander builds a custom agent for you.

<details>
<summary><b>All 16 built-in agents</b></summary>

| Area | Agent | What it delivers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research & analysis | **DeepResearcher** | Evidence-grounded research with verified sources, flagged contradictions and an auditable report |
| | **SeoGeoAgent** | Give it a URL — technical audit, content quality, Core Web Vitals, AI-answer (GEO) citability, ranked fix list |
| | **StockAnalyser** | Equity research, factor screens, backtests and portfolio risk checks, with traceable dashboards |
| Content & media | **ContentWriter** | Publish-ready posts, articles, newsletters and case studies from a goal, sources or a rough draft |
| | **PptMaker** | Editable, reviewable PPTX decks from a topic, outline or document |
| | **ImageStudio** | Posters, covers, social images and infographics |
| | **VideoStudio** | Narration, AI presenters, captions and dubbing, highlight clips, localization, and reference-video recreation with your own content and footage |
| | **VoiceStudio** | Narration, multi-voice audio, transcripts and subtitles, audio editing and mixing |
| | **UIDesigner** | Editable, HTML-first UI from product goals, PRDs, screenshots or Figma material |
| Build & office | **ProductDeveloper** | Repo-aware engineering — implement a PRD, fix bugs, refactor, review, with verifiable results |
| | **OfficeWorker** | Create, edit, check and deliver Word / Excel / PowerPoint / PDF files, one at a time or in batches |
| E-commerce | **ECommerceResearcher** | Product selection by budget, market and sourcing limits — candidates, rejection reasons, validation plans |
| | **ECommerceWriter** | Titles, detail pages, FAQs, image copy and video scripts in your brand voice |
| | **ECommerceReviewer** | Review and reputation analysis — customer themes, root causes of bad reviews, priorities |

More on each agent → [orkas.ai/agents](https://orkas.ai/agents/?source=gh-orkas)

</details>

### Recreate a reference video with your own content

**VideoStudio** can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Supply a reference video file and your assets: the agent analyzes the hook, information order, visual beats and call to action, then proposes what to preserve and what to replace before production.

This works best for motion-graphic explainers, SaaS or app demos, and product ads built from your existing footage. Locally authored text, captions, narration and clips can be revised separately; text baked into AI-generated footage requires changing that footage.

> "Use reference.mp4 as a reference for a 30-second vertical promo. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first."

Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the [reference-recreation workflow](./resources/builtin/marketplace/agents/79df9cc89f5f/skills/video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md).

---

## Keep the work moving

One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going.

- **Projects** — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch.
- **To-dos and Auto-advance** — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review.
- **Scheduled automations** — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. Orkas runs on your computer. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts.
- **Connectors** — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything.
- **Apps** — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link.
- **Shared projects** *(packaged app)* — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent.

> [!NOTE]
> Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, **[download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** (free, with 500 credits to start).

Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an **Orkas API Key** in **Settings → Models**, then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings.

---

## Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together

Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents **Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode**, and the personal agents **OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent**. The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way.

[Using Claude Code and Codex together →](https://orkas.ai/blog/claude-code-codex-together/?source=gh-orkas)

---

## Why Orkas

- **A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest** — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit.
- **Local-first by design** — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service.
- **Any model, switch any time** — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings.
- **Agents that get better** — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills.
- **Open source, no black box** — MIT licensed. Read exactly what Orkas and every agent and skill do.

> ⭐ If Orkas is useful to you, a star helps more people find the project.

## What people use it for

- **Marketing content** — launch videos, product pages, posts and newsletters in your voice. [Content writing](https://orkas.ai/use/content-writing/?source=gh-orkas) · [Videos](https://orkas.ai/use/make-videos/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Store operations** — weekly sales briefs, review replies, listings and competitor checks. [E-commerce](https://orkas.ai/use/ecommerce/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Research and reports** — sourced reports and decks, on demand or every week. [Research](https://orkas.ai/use/researchers/?source=gh-orkas) · [Data analysis](https://orkas.ai/use/data-analysis/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Chat with your documents** — answers grounded in your own files, with citations back to the source passages. [Chat with documents](https://orkas.ai/use/chat-with-documents/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Client work** — meeting briefs, monthly client reports and update decks in your template. [Monthly client report template](https://orkas.ai/blog/monthly-client-report-template/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Product launch** — landing pages, bug fixes with tests, changelogs and launch posts. [Developers](https://orkas.ai/use/developers/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Build an app** — quote calculators, booking forms, internal tools. [Build apps](https://orkas.ai/use/build-apps/?source=gh-orkas)
- **Small teams** — one project for people and agents. [Small teams](https://orkas.ai/use/small-teams/?source=gh-orkas)

---

## How Orkas compares

| Tool | What it is | How Orkas differs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Claude Code** | Anthropic's agentic coding tool — in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, built on Claude models. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Claude Code as one of its agents. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. [Orkas vs Claude Code →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code/?source=gh-orkas) |
| **Codex** | OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. [Orkas vs Codex →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex/?source=gh-orkas) |
| **LangChain** | A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app. | Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default. |
| **CrewAI** | A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code. | Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in. |
| **OpenClaw** | A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents. | Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent. |
| **Hermes-Agent** | Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app. | Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them. |

**Orkas is for you if** you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk.

**Not for you if** you just want a single all-purpose chatbot, or a pure code library to embed in your own app.

**Choosing between coding agents?** [Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code vs Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-vs-codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code alternatives](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-alternatives/?source=gh-orkas)

**Full side-by-side comparisons →** [vs Claude Code](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Codex](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Cline](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-cline?source=gh-orkas) · [vs LangChain](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-langchain?source=gh-orkas) · [vs ChatGPT](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-chatgpt?source=gh-orkas) · [vs OpenClaw](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-openclaw?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Hermes-Agent](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-hermes-agent?source=gh-orkas)

---

## Quick start

Want a packaged installer instead? See [Download](#download) above. To run from source — currently the way to run Orkas on Linux:

**Requirements**: Node 22.12+ · macOS / Windows 10+ / glibc 2.34+ Linux x64 or arm64. Keep Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain available for the uncommon native-module source-build fallback.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas.git
cd Orkas
./run.sh           # macOS / Linux
run.cmd            # Windows
```

Linux source runs require glibc 2.34+. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. Local speech transcription downloads and verifies the target-native whisper.cpp runtime and multilingual model during the first source launch.

`run.sh` / `run.cmd` installs the locked npm dependency tree and prepares the pinned Python, uv, Node, embedding model (~95 MB), OfficeCLI, FFmpeg, whisper.cpp, and multilingual speech model resources on first launch. Linux startup then verifies the platform-native modules and Whisper runtime under Electron's ABI before opening the app. OCR and Skill-specific Python packages are installed into isolated local environments when those features are first used. First launch creates a workspace under `~/.orkas/` (macOS / Linux) or `<smallest non-system drive>:\.orkas\` (Windows). Then open **Settings → AI Providers** to add an API key or OAuth.

Native dependency errors: use Node.js 24 LTS (minimum 22.12.0), then run
`npm run native:repair` from this checkout. This restores optional packages,
repairs SQLite for Electron, prepares bundled Node for isolated image processing,
and checks SQL, sqlite-vec and sharp before success.
Use `npm run native:check` for a check without installation.
See the [native dependency verification script](./scripts/verify-native-dependencies.cjs) for the checks performed.

---

## How it works

### Task routing

The Commander handles general work itself and delegates specialist work through three tools:

- **`dispatch_to`** runs a named agent and returns its result for continued work. It can wait for the result or run asynchronously and notify the Commander when the task finishes.
- **`hand_off_to`** transfers the remaining work to a named agent and ends the current Commander turn. The agent delivers its own reply; an optional continuation lets the Commander resume a broader task afterward.
- **`run_worker`** runs an anonymous, isolated sub-task and returns a private result. It does not receive conversation history or a named agent's skills.

Named agent tasks and anonymous workers have separate concurrency controls. See the [dispatch implementation](./src/main/features/group_chat/bus.ts) and [execution locks](./src/main/util/locks.ts).

### Context management

The runtime budgets context against the selected model's usable input capacity, accounting for prompts, tools and persistent runtime state. Completed dialogue uses a bounded recent-history window; long active tasks use checkpoints to condense earlier process messages while retaining recent work. File reads, file changes and command executions also have structured records that can survive context compaction.

See [context budgets](./src/core-agent/src/agent/context-budget.ts), [session history and checkpoints](./src/core-agent/src/agent/session.ts) and [workspace records](./src/core-agent/src/agent/workspace-state.ts).

### Memory and the Library

Durable notes keep user preferences, project facts and each agent's reusable knowledge in separate scopes. These notes are distinct from the Library's document index and the stored conversation history.

The Library extracts documents into passages and stores a local SQLite vector index. Its embedding model runs on your machine; the `library` tool can list files, search relevant passages and read source content from the global or current-project Library. Earlier conversations are retrieved separately through `chat_history`.

See [scoped memory](./src/main/features/memory.ts), [document extraction](./src/main/util/file_to_chunks.ts), [Library tools](./src/main/model/core-agent/kb-tools.ts) and [conversation retrieval](./src/main/model/core-agent/chat-history-tools.ts).

README

# Agent Skills

**Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.**

Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development.

<a href="https://trendshift.io/repositories/25200" target="_blank"><img src="https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/25200" alt="addyosmani%2Fagent-skills | Trendshift" style="width: 250px; height: 55px;" width="250" height="55"/></a>

![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg)

```
  DEFINE          PLAN           BUILD          VERIFY         REVIEW          SHIP
 ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐      ┌──────┐
 │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │  QA  │ ───▶ │  Go  │
 │Refine│      │  PRD │      │ Impl │      │Debug │      │ Gate │      │ Live │
 └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘      └──────┘
  /spec          /plan          /build        /test         /review       /ship
```

---

## Commands

9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically.

| What you're doing | Command | Key principle |
|-------------------|---------|---------------|
| Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code |
| Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks |
| Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time |
| Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof |
| Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere |
| Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health |
| Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize |
| Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness |
| Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer |

In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`.

Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps.

Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on.

---

## Quick Start

**Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more):

```bash
npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills            # install all 25 skills
npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list     # browse before installing
```

Or grab individual skills:

```bash
npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality   # five-axis review before merge
npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me              # requirements interrogation, one question at a time
npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development   # red-green-refactor, enforced
```

> **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only
> `skills/<name>/`, not the repo-level `references/` directory. The skill still
> works, but paths to supplementary shared checklists are unavailable. Use a
> whole-repo integration, clone the repository, or copy the needed checklist into
> a `references/` directory inside the installed skill. This portability gap is
> tracked in [#361](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/issues/361).

Prefer a native integration? Pick your tool below.

<details>
<summary><b>Claude Code (recommended)</b></summary>

**Marketplace install:**

```
/plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills
/plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills
```

> **SSH errors?** The marketplace clones repos via SSH. If you don't have SSH keys set up on GitHub, either [add your SSH key](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account) or use the full HTTPS URL to force HTTPS cloning during the marketplace-add step:
> ```bash
> /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git
> /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills
> ```
>
> If `/plugin install` still fails with `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` on Windows or macOS, the recommended workaround is to configure Git once to rewrite GitHub SSH URLs to HTTPS for subprocess clones:
> ```bash
> git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com:
> ```

**Local / development:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git
claude --plugin-dir /path/to/agent-skills
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Cursor</b></summary>

Put workflow skills under `.cursor/skills/` (sync from `agent-skills/skills/`) and short policies in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` — do not paste full skills into rules. Both directories live in your project; this repo does not ship a `.cursor/` folder. See [docs/cursor-setup.md](docs/cursor-setup.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Antigravity CLI</b></summary>

Install as a native plugin for skills and subagents. In affected Antigravity CLI releases, legacy command TOMLs are reported as converted but their wrapper commands are not discoverable; invoke the underlying namespaced skills directly. See [docs/antigravity-setup.md](docs/antigravity-setup.md#lifecycle-workflows-and-command-compatibility).

**Install from the repo:**

```bash
agy plugin install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git
```

**Install from a local clone:**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git
agy plugin install ./agent-skills
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Gemini CLI</b></summary>

Install as native skills for auto-discovery, or add to `GEMINI.md` for persistent context. See [docs/gemini-cli-setup.md](docs/gemini-cli-setup.md).

**Install from the repo:**

```bash
gemini skills install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git --path skills
```

**Install from a local clone:**

```bash
gemini skills install ./agent-skills/skills/
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Windsurf</b></summary>

Add skill contents to your Windsurf rules configuration. See [docs/windsurf-setup.md](docs/windsurf-setup.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>OpenCode</b></summary>

Copy skills to `.opencode/skills/` (or `~/.config/opencode/skills/`), add a project-local `AGENTS.md`, and use the built-in `skill` tool for agent-driven execution. Optional slash commands can be added under `.opencode/commands/`.

See [docs/opencode-setup.md](docs/opencode-setup.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>GitHub Copilot</b></summary>

Use agent definitions from `agents/` as Copilot personas and skill content in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The lifecycle slash commands (`/spec`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/test`, `/review`, `/ship`) are Claude Code commands and do not appear in Copilot; invoke the skills by name (`/spec-driven-development`, …) instead. Already installed? How you roll the pack out depends on your codebase. The **[Adoption Guide](docs/adoption-guide.md)** covers two paths: the full lifecycle from day one for a greenfield project, or an incremental, verification-first rollout for an established codebase.

## How Skills Work

Every skill follows a consistent anatomy:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SKILL.md                                       │
│                                                 │
│  ┌─ Frontmatter ─────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ name: lowercase-hyphen-name               │  │
│  │ description: Guides agents through [task].│  │
│  │              Use when…                    │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────┘  │                                                                                                
│  Overview         → What this skill does        │
│  When to Use      → Triggering conditions       │
│  Process          → Step-by-step workflow       │

│  Red Flags        → Signs something's wrong     │
│  Verification     → Evidence requirements       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key design choices:**

- **Process, not prose.** Skills are workflows agents follow, not reference docs they read. Each has steps, checkpoints, and exit criteria.

## What is Fleetbase?

Fleetbase is an open-source, modular operating system for logistics and supply chain operations. It covers dispatch, fleet management, live tracking, commerce, warehousing, and finance in one platform, with a REST API, webhooks, and an extension system for everything else. Run it on your own infrastructure or use [Fleetbase Cloud](https://console.fleetbase.io/onboard).

## Who Uses Fleetbase

Fleetbase is built for teams that move goods, people, or equipment and want to own the software that runs it. Because every workflow, field, and status is configurable, the same platform adapts to very different operations.

| Industry | How Fleetbase is used |
|----------|-----------------------|
| [Trucking & Haulage](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/trucking) | Replace a legacy TMS with real-time tracking, route optimization, and digital proof of delivery. |
| [Courier & Parcel](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/courier-services) | Automate dispatch, raise first-attempt delivery rates, and give customers live parcel tracking. |
| [Food & Grocery Delivery](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/food-delivery) | Run on-demand delivery with instant dispatch, live customer tracking, and automated notifications. |
| [E‑commerce & Retail](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/ecommerce) | Power same-day and next-day delivery and returns through a headless API. |
| [Healthcare & Pharmacy](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/healthcare) | Track chain of custody and prioritize urgent deliveries with full audit trails. |
| [Waste & Recycling](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/waste-management) | Optimize collection routes, track containers, and produce compliance reports. |
| [Container Operations](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/container-operations) | Follow containers across multi-modal journeys from port to door. |
| [Government & Defense](https://fleetbase.io/solutions/government) | Self-host with role-based access, full audit trails, and complete data sovereignty. |

Developers use Fleetbase as a foundation too, building custom logistics products on its API and extension framework.

## Platform

Fleetbase is made up of modules that install into the console as extensions. Each one works on its own and integrates with the rest.

| Module | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| [Fleet‑Ops](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/fleet-ops) | Fleet management and dispatch: orders, drivers, vehicles, live tracking, route optimization, configurable workflows, and maintenance. |
| [Storefront](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/storefront) | Headless commerce for on-demand businesses, with multi-vendor marketplaces and native Fleet-Ops delivery. |
| [Pallet](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/pallet) | Warehouse management for inventory, pick lists, cycle counts, and fulfilment. |
| [Ledger](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/ledger) | Invoicing, payments, wallets, and accounting for logistics operators. |
| [Customer Portal](https://github.com/fleetbase/customer-portal) | A self-service workspace for your customers to place and track orders, get quotes and pay, view invoices, manage documents, and open support tickets. |
| [AI](https://fleetbase.io/platform/ai) | Natural-language order creation, operational queries, and order insights powered by OpenAI or Claude. |
| [IAM](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/identity-and-access/users) | Identity and access management: users, groups, roles, policies, and two-factor authentication across your organization. |
| [Developers](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/developer-console) | The developer console: API keys, webhooks, socket and system events, and request logs, with separate test and live environments. |
| [Navigator App](https://github.com/fleetbase/navigator-app) | Open-source driver app for iOS and Android with real-time dispatch, navigation, and proof of delivery. |
| [Storefront App](https://github.com/fleetbase/storefront-app) | Open-source iOS and Android app for launching your own shop or marketplace. |

| **Extensible** | Install extensions from the marketplace or build your own to add features directly into the OS. |
| **Developer friendly** | REST API, WebSockets, and webhooks for integrating external systems or building custom apps. |
| **Configurable workflows** | Define order types with their own activity flows, custom fields, and automation. |

| **Internationalized** | Translate the console into any language. |

Fleetbase has two open-source mobile apps, both built with React Native. They connect to Fleetbase Cloud or to your own self-hosted instance, and you can rebrand them and publish them to the App Store and Google Play under your own name.

- An **Inbox** for order threads and messages from dispatch.

There are three ways to run Fleetbase:

- **[Fleetbase Cloud](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/quickstart/cloud-quickstart)**: fully managed, with nothing to install. [Start a free trial](https://console.fleetbase.io/onboard).
- **[Run locally](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/quickstart/running-locally)**: self-host with Docker on your own machine or server.
- **[Deploy in your cloud](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/quickstart/deploy-in-cloud)**: run production workloads on AWS, GCP, Azure, or any other provider.

### Quickstart

You need Docker with Docker Compose v2, Git, Node.js 18 or newer, and at least 4 GB of RAM allocated to Docker. Then install the Fleetbase CLI and run the interactive installer:

```bash
npm install -g @fleetbase/cli
flb install-fleetbase
```

When setup finishes, open the console at http://localhost:4200 and create your first admin account and organization. The API is served at http://localhost:8000.

The [running locally guide](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/quickstart/running-locally) also covers installing with Docker Compose or the setup script, configuring services like mail, maps, and SMS, and troubleshooting. To work on Fleetbase itself, follow the [development setup guide](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/quickstart/development-setup).

## Releases

Every [release](https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/releases) publishes Docker images. It also attaches standalone binaries and a performance report to the release, and refreshes the database diagram in this repository.

### Standalone binaries

Each release attaches a single-file build of the Fleetbase API for Linux and macOS:

| Platform | Download |
|----------|----------|
| Linux (x86_64) | [`fleetbase-linux-x86_64`](https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/releases/latest/download/fleetbase-linux-x86_64) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | [`fleetbase-darwin-arm64`](https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/releases/latest/download/fleetbase-darwin-arm64) |

Each binary is a static [FrankenPHP](https://frankenphp.dev/docs/embed/) build. It bundles the API, PHP and every PHP extension Fleetbase needs (including GEOS for geospatial queries), along with the web server. You don't need PHP or Composer on the machine. You still need MySQL and Redis, configured through the API's usual environment variables, and the console is served separately. Docker remains the recommended way to run Fleetbase in production.

```bash
chmod +x fleetbase-linux-x86_64
./fleetbase-linux-x86_64 php-cli artisan migrate   # run Artisan commands
./fleetbase-linux-x86_64 php-server                # serve the API
```

### Performance report

Each release also attaches a performance report: `performance-report-<version>.html` and `.md`, with the raw numbers in `performance-metrics-<version>.json`. [Open the latest release](https://github.com/fleetbase/fleetbase/releases/latest) to see it.

The report comes from a [k6](https://k6.io) benchmark ([`tests/k6/api-release.js`](tests/k6/api-release.js)) run against a fresh stack booted from source:

- **Throughput.** Ramping load across the public API: orders, places, contacts, drivers, vehicles, fleets and more. It reports average, p50, p90, p95 and p99 latency, requests per second and error rate overall, for reads and writes, and per endpoint. Every figure is compared with the previous release.
- **Rate-limit isolation.** One API key floods the API far past its limit while a second organization and the console keep working. The second organization and the console must get zero `429` responses.

Release pull requests run the same benchmark as a check. Errors and broken rate-limit isolation always fail it. A latency regression fails it only when it's both large and confirmed by a second run. The benchmark runs on a GitHub-hosted runner, so treat the numbers as a comparison between releases, not a prediction of production throughput.

### Database schema (ERD)

[`erd.svg`](erd.svg) is an entity relationship diagram of the full Fleetbase database: core, Fleet‑Ops, Storefront and the other bundled extensions. A [dark version](erd-dark.svg) is also available. A workflow regenerates both from the migrations on every release branch and opens a pull request with the update, so the diagram always matches the latest release.

## Extensions

Extensions add features, integrate external systems, or change how Fleetbase behaves. Browse and install them from the console or with the [Fleetbase CLI](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/cli), and publish your own to the marketplace as free or paid extensions.

- [Browse and install extensions](https://www.fleetbase.io/docs/platform/extensions/browsing-and-installing)

# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

<p align="left">
  <strong>English</strong> · <a href="README_ZH.md">简体中文 (Chinese)</a>
</p>

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History**

[**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en)

*The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en">
    <img src="assets/hero_demo_en.webp" alt="Chronicles of the Realm — 15s Interactive Overview (Warring States Unification, 2,400-Year Dynastic Scrubbing, Chang'an Place Genealogy & Su Shi's Exile Route)" width="100%" />
  </a>
</p>

---

## Why It's Fun to Explore

Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry:
- *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"*
- *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"*
- *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"*

**Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time.

---

### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders

- **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to zoom straight to it.
- **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Hami & Seven Guards West of Jiayuguan (1404 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible.
- **Inline Reigning Monarch & Imperial Era Display**: The timeline dynamically displays the reigning monarch (temple/posthumous title + personal name + reign span, e.g., `Emperor Wu of Han · Liu Che`, `Emperor Taizong of Tang · Li Shimin`, `Emperor Shengzu of Qing · Xuanye`) alongside the exact imperial era year.
- **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern X-Ray Lens**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents, or toggle the **X-Ray Lens** to project modern provincial boundaries directly over the historical map.
- **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era.

> [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Prefecture" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75&center=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Prefecture&lang=en)

![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp)

---

### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`)

**Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card:
- **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Imperial Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks.
- **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Key Events`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year!
- **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*.

> [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en)

![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp)

---

### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space

Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, plotting every milestone of their life with delicate cartographic hairline arcs and directional ticks across changing dynastic borders:
- **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map!
- **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi.
- **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains.
- **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an.
- **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu.
- **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island.
- **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an.

Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site.

> [Try It Live: Follow Su Dongpo's Exile to Mizhou & Huangzhou (1075–1082 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en)

![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp)

---

### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn?

Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**):
- **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the on-pin **`✓ Confirm`** button to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates!
- Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**.

> [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en)

![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp)

---

## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links

### Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key / Action | Effect |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** |
| **`←` / `→`** or bottom **`‹ / ›`** | Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold `Shift + ← / →` to step by `10` years) |
| **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) |
| **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes |
| **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location |
| **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to auto-zoom to its bounding box |

### Shareable Deep Links

Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route:
- **Jump to a specific year or territorial shift**: [`?year=-403&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-403&lang=en) (403 BCE · Partition of Jin) / [`?year=-121&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&lang=en) (121 BCE · Huo Qubing opens the Hexi Corridor) / [`?year=648&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=648&lang=en) (648 CE · Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance in India) / [`?year=1288&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1288&lang=en) (1288 CE · Yuan Xuanzhengyuan over Tibet) / [`?year=1881&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1881&lang=en) (1881 CE · Zeng Jize recovers Ili) / [`?year=1945&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1945&lang=en) (1945 CE · Retrocession of Taiwan)
- **Pinpoint a famous battle**: [`?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en) (Battle of Changping) / [`?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en) (Battle of Red Cliffs) / [`?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en) (Battle of Fei River)
- **Inspect a city's 2,400-year genealogy**: [`?year=741&place=长安&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=长安&lang=en) (Chang'an / Xi'an) / [`?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en) (Jiankang / Yingtian / Nanjing) / [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en) (Han Yu at Languan Pass)
- **Plot a custom poetic or campaign route**: [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en) (Du Fu's 763 CE homeward route) / [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en) (Su Shi's multi-year exile route across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou, and Danzhou)

- **Start a quiz round**: [`?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) (Map Pinpoint Challenge)
- **Switch UI language**: [`?lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) (English) / [`?lang=zh-tw`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw) (Traditional Chinese) / [`/`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/) (Simplified Chinese)

### Embed in Your Page

Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site:

1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see.
2. Copy the URL and add `&embed=1`.
3. Paste it into an `<iframe>`:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?embed=1&year=1104&trace=101.778,36.617&from=1072&to=1126&lang=en"
  width="100%" height="480" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
  title="Chronicles of the Realm · 1104 CE, Northern Song"></iframe>
```

The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map.

| Parameter | Effect |
|---|---|
| `embed=1` | Turn on embed mode (required) |
| `year`, `polity`, `person`, `stop`, `trace`, `lang` | Same as the share links above |
| `from=1072&to=1126` | Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it |
| `lock=1` | Freeze the map at `year` and hide the timeline |
| `autoplay=1` | Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with `person`), or play the timeline |

WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead.

---

## AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration

**Chronicles of the Realm** works out of the box as a **historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents**. Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card:

- **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt)
- **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`:
  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "jiangshan-atlas": {
        "command": "node",
        "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"]
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies):
  - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL.
  - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL.
  - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones.
- **Ready-to-Use Agent Skill**: [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md) (includes the zero-dependency CLI renderer [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py))

## Install ECC

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ECC 2.2 includes guided package setup for Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code.
> The universal package requires Node.js 18 or newer. Claude plugin setup also
> requires Git and Claude Code 2.1 or newer on `PATH`.

### Recommended: universal guided setup

For Claude Code plugin setup, updates, scope changes, and hook-profile changes:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup
```

#### Windows first-time walkthrough

If you are new to command-line tools, use this copy-and-paste path:

1. Install Node.js 18 or newer, Git, and Claude Code.
2. Open **PowerShell** from the Windows Start menu.
3. Confirm that each prerequisite is available:

   ```powershell
   node --version
   git --version
   claude --version
   ```

4. Run the guided installer:

   ```powershell
   npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup
   ```

5. For a typical personal setup, choose **Global user**, choose **Standard** hooks, and confirm.
6. Start a new Claude Code session and run `/plugin list` to verify that `ecc@ecc` is enabled.

This path does not require cloning the repository. If any prerequisite command is not found, install or repair that prerequisite before rerunning ECC setup.

If npm reports a version or cache error, confirm the registry version before retrying:

```bash
npm view ecc-universal version
```

ECC 2.2 supports the same guided setup through modern package runners:

| Package runner | Guided setup command |
|---|---|
| npm / npx | `npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| pnpm | `pnpm dlx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| Yarn 2+ | `yarn dlx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| Bun | `bunx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |

The examples select [the published ECC 2.2.3 release](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ecc-universal/v/2.2.3), matching this repository's release version. A version pin is not a security audit or an integrity check. Review the release source and registry integrity before running package code; use a reviewed checkout for unreleased changes.

Yarn Classic 1 does not provide `yarn dlx`; use `npx`, install the package globally, or upgrade Yarn for a temporary one-shot run.

The wizard inventories the official marketplace and every native Claude install scope before making changes, then installs, updates, or safely moves `ecc@ecc` to the scope you choose. Rerun the same command whenever you want to update ECC, change scope, or change its hook profile. This setup wizard currently configures the Claude Code plugin; use the multi-harness wizard below for Codex or Kimi Code.

To configure more than one coding agent in one reviewed flow, use the multi-harness wizard:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided
```

It lets you select any combination of Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code, shows each install channel and destination, preflights every selection before the first write, and asks for one final confirmation.

| Harness | Guided install behavior |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Native `ecc@ecc` plugin with one `user`, `project`, or `local` scope and an ECC hook profile |
| Codex | Native Codex marketplace/plugin lifecycle; hook review and trust remain Codex-owned |
| Kimi Code | Managed project files under `./.kimi-code`; ECC hooks, model/provider settings, and authentication are not configured |

For automation, make every provider-specific choice explicit:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided \
  --harness claude --harness codex --harness kimi \
  --claude-scope local --claude-hooks standard \
  --profile core --yes
```

Verify the native guided Codex path and managed Kimi path without writing first:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided --harness codex --dry-run
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --profile core --target kimi --dry-run
```

Additional package-name commands are also available through the 2.2 alias:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 consult "security reviews" --target claude
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --profile minimal --target claude --with capability:machine-learning
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 doctor --target kimi
```

Do not use `npx ecc-install --profile minimal --target claude`: `ecc-install` is a binary name inside `ecc-universal`, not a separately published npm package.

ECC also ships advanced managed adapters for `cursor`, `antigravity`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `codebuddy`, `joycode`, `qwen`, `zed`, `hermes`, and `openclaw`. Those targets still use their documented `ecc install --target ...` paths until each adapter has passed the guided collision, update, repair, and uninstall lifecycle matrix. Neither wizard silently installs into every detected harness.

### Pick one path only (per harness)

You can use ECC with Claude Code, Codex, and other harnesses at the same time. Choose one install method for each harness:

- **Recommended default:** run the guided Claude plugin setup above
- **Also supported for Claude Code:** use the [native plugin commands](#claude-code-details)
- **Available in release 2.2:** guided package setup for Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code
- **Works:** Claude Code plugin + Codex native plugin
- **Works:** Claude Code plugin + the legacy Codex sync flow
- **Avoid:** Claude Code plugin + full Claude manual install
- **Avoid:** Codex sync + Codex marketplace plugin

**Do not stack install methods.** Installing ECC twice into the same harness can duplicate skills, commands, hooks, or configuration; installing it once into multiple harnesses does not.

If you already layered multiple installs and things look duplicated, skip straight to [Reset / Uninstall ECC](#reset--uninstall-ecc).

**Install trouble?** Open the short [install or runtime problem form](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/issues/new?template=install-problem.yml), or run `ecc feedback`. ECC never uploads diagnostics automatically.

### Claude Code details

Alternatively, run Claude Code's native plugin commands inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC
/plugin install ecc@ecc
```

The native path installs ECC's skills, agents, commands, and plugin-managed hooks. If you choose it, stop there. Do not also run a full manual install into Claude Code.

Claude Code owns these built-in commands, including their errors when a marketplace, plugin, or conflicting scope already exists. ECC cannot intercept that parser. If either native command reports an existing install or scope conflict, use the 2.2 guided setup or resolve the conflicting Claude plugin scope before retrying; do not layer a manual install on top.

After ECC is installed, `/ecc:configure-ecc` is the namespaced in-Claude reconfiguration skill. It delegates to the same safe setup flow, but it is available only after the plugin is installed and cannot replace Claude Code's built-in `/plugin` command during a first install.

Claude Code plugins cannot distribute `rules`, so add only the rule packs you actually want:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC.git
cd ECC
mkdir -p ~/.claude/rules/ecc
cp -R rules/common ~/.claude/rules/ecc/
cp -R rules/typescript ~/.claude/rules/ecc/  # replace with your stack
```

Start with `rules/common` plus one language or framework pack you actually use. If you install the plugin, do not run `./install.sh --profile full` afterward.

<details>
<summary><strong>Prefer settings.json? Add the marketplace declaratively</strong></summary>

Add directly to your `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "ecc": {
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "affaan-m/ECC"
      }
    }
  },

    "ecc@ecc": true
  }
}
```

This gives you the same result as the two `/plugin` commands above.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Naming + migration note (ecc@ecc, affaan-m/ECC, ecc-universal)</strong></summary>

ECC has three public identifiers, and they are not interchangeable:

- GitHub source repo: `affaan-m/ECC`
- Claude marketplace/plugin identifier: `ecc@ecc`
- npm package: `ecc-universal`

This is intentional. Anthropic marketplace/plugin installs are keyed by a canonical plugin identifier, so ECC uses `ecc@ecc` to keep tool names and slash-command namespaces short enough for strict Desktop/API validators. Older posts may still show the former long marketplace identifier; treat that as a legacy alias only. Separately, the npm package stayed on `ecc-universal`, so npm installs and marketplace installs intentionally use different names.

npm releases are cut per version tag, not per commit, so `ecc-universal` tracks releases (2.1, 2.2, ...) rather than every push to `main`. Install from git if you want the bleeding edge.

If your local Claude setup was wiped or reset, that does not mean you need to repurchase anything. Start with `node scripts/ecc.js list-installed`, then run `node scripts/ecc.js doctor` and `node scripts/ecc.js repair` before reinstalling. That usually restores ECC-managed files without rebuilding your setup.

**Portable AI Studio** is a completely offline, zero-setup, self-contained AI studio for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Unlike cloud-based AI systems, it runs entirely on your own hardware with no censorship, tracking, subscriptions, or login requirements.

It unifies four major local AI capabilities into one high-performance desktop interface:
1. **🎨 Image Generation (Stable Diffusion):** Generate and edit high-quality images offline using `.safetensors`, `.gguf`, or `.ckpt` model weights.
2. **💬 Text Chat (LLMs):** Converse privately with open-source language models (GGUF format) powered by official, high-performance `llama.cpp` backends.
3. **🎙️ Speech-to-Text (Whisper):** Transcribe voice recordings and speech to text in real-time with an integrated `whisper.cpp` engine.
4. **🗣️ Text-to-Speech (Kokoro TTS):** Convert text outputs into highly natural, lifelike vocal audio offline using the `Kokoro-82M` ONNX model.

---

## <a id="key-features"></a>🌟 Key Features

*   **100% Offline & Private:** Run inferences locally. No internet, telemetry, cloud logging, or API keys required.
*   **Zero-Install Portability:** Entire runtime (Node.js, models, GPU backends) is self-contained. Zero global system environment changes.
*   **Auto-Configured Acceleration:** Auto-detects hardware specs to load CUDA (Nvidia), ROCm (AMD), Vulkan (Intel/AMD/NVIDIA), Metal (macOS), or OpenVINO (Intel NPU) backends.
*   **Integrated Model Manager:** Paste Hugging Face URLs to download weights directly, or drag-and-drop local weights to import them.
*   **Live Performance Monitor:** Track CPU, RAM, GPU, and VRAM utilization in real-time directly inside the web UI.
*   **Local Output Gallery:** Saves generated images side-by-side with prompt parameters and metadata JSON files.

---

## <a id="workspace-architecture"></a>⚙️ Workspace & Engine Architecture

To avoid exhausting system RAM or VRAM, text and image engines are mutually exclusive by default. You can switch between workspaces inside the UI:

*   **Image Generation Workspace:** Uses a dedicated `stable-diffusion.cpp` backend node. Model weights are stored in `app/models/`.
*   **Text Chat Workspace:** Uses a portable `llama.cpp` server backend. Model weights (.gguf) are stored in `app/llm-models/`. A small Qwen2.5 Coder starter model can be downloaded directly from the Text Chat panel.
*   **Speech Worker (Whisper):** Runs a localized `whisper-cli` process to convert your vocal input to text.
*   **Audio Output (Kokoro TTS):** Utilizes `kokoro-js` locally on the server side to read responses in natural voices.

---

## <a id="supported-models"></a>Supported Models

The app is designed around single-file local models that can be loaded directly by the bundled backend engines.

### Image generation

| Model type | Supported | Put files in | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Stable Diffusion 1.5 checkpoints | Yes | `app/models/` | Best compatibility. Use `.safetensors` or `.ckpt` files. |
| SDXL checkpoints | Yes | `app/models/` | Supported as single-file checkpoints. Requires more RAM/VRAM than SD 1.5. |
| Single-file SD/SDXL GGUF checkpoints | Limited | `app/models/` | Only complete single-file checkpoints are supported. |
| OpenVINO image model folders | Intel NPU only | `app/openvino-models/` | Download from the Model Manager after running the OpenVINO setup. |
| CoreML image models | Apple Silicon only | `app/models/` | Requires macOS on Apple Silicon and the CoreML setup path. |
| Flux, HiDream, Hunyuan, Wan, Qwen Image, Z-Image workflows | No | N/A | These usually require separate diffusion, VAE, and text encoder files and are not one-click checkpoint loads in this app. |
| LoRA, ControlNet, VAE-only, text-encoder-only, or diffusion-only files | No | N/A | Companion files are not loaded as standalone image models. |

Known-good image models available from the Model Manager:

| Name | Filename | Type | Approx. size | Recommended use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Juggernaut XL v9 Lightning | `Juggernaut_RunDiffusionPhoto2_Lightning_4Steps.safetensors` | SDXL | 7.1 GB | High-quality photorealism on mid/high tier machines. |
| DreamShaper XL Lightning | `DreamShaperXL_Lightning.safetensors` | SDXL | 6.9 GB | General SDXL images, fantasy, renders, and illustration. |
| DreamShaper 8 | `DreamShaper_8_pruned.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.1 GB | Faster, lower-memory image generation. |
| CyberRealistic V8 | `CyberRealistic_V8_FP16.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.0 GB | Realistic SD 1.5 images and lower-memory systems. |
| Rev Animated | `rev-animated-v1-2-2.safetensors` | SD 1.5 | 2.0 GB | Stylized/anime SD 1.5 images. |
| LCM DreamShaper OpenVINO | `OpenVINO/LCM_Dreamshaper_v7-fp16-ov` | OpenVINO | 2.7 GB | Intel Core Ultra NPU test model. |

### Text, speech, and TTS

| Workspace | Supported model files | Put files in | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Text Chat | `.gguf` llama.cpp models | `app/llm-models/` | Use single-file GGUF chat/instruct models. Vision models may also require a matching `mmproj` file. |
| Speech-to-Text | whisper.cpp `.bin` models | `app/speech-models/` | Use Whisper GGML/whisper.cpp model files. |
| Text-to-Speech | Kokoro `.json` manifests and model assets | `app/tts-models/` / `app/tts-runtime/` | Use the built-in Kokoro setup and Model Manager entries. |

> Linux release binaries are built for Ubuntu 24.04-era systems and require `glibc 2.38+` plus `GLIBCXX_3.4.32+`. On older Ubuntu/Debian VMs, a model such as CyberRealistic may be valid but the backend can still fail before loading it. Upgrade the VM OS or build the backend from source.

## <a id="getting-started"></a>🚀 Getting Started

Ensure you have a modern web browser installed. Follow the quick guide below for your platform:

### Windows Setup

1. **Launch:** Double-click **`windows.bat`**.
   > [!NOTE]
   > On the first run, the script will automatically download a portable Node.js runtime and configure pre-compiled GPU/CPU backend binaries.
2. **Add Models:** Drop `.safetensors`, `.gguf`, or `.ckpt` weights into `app/models/` (or download them via the **Model Manager** tab in the UI).
3. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser, select your model, and write a prompt.

### Linux Setup

1. **Make executable:** Open a terminal in the project folder and make the script executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x linux.sh
   ```
2. **Launch:** Run **`./linux.sh`**.
   - **NVIDIA GPU Users:** You will be prompted to set up the high-performance **CUDA** backend (downloads prebuilt or automatically compiles from source as a fallback).
   - **AMD Radeon Performance:** Run with **`./linux.sh --max-perf`** to add the ROCm backend (~1.3 GB download).
   - **Intel Core Ultra NPU:** Run with **`./linux.sh --setup-openvino`** to configure Intel NPU support (requires Intel Linux NPU driver).
3. **Add Models:** Drop your weights into `app/models/` or download them via the **Model Manager** tab.
4. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser.

### macOS Setup

1. **Make executable:** Open a terminal in the project folder and make the script executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x mac.sh
   ```
2. **Launch:** Run **`./mac.sh`**.
   > [!IMPORTANT]
   > The prebuilt macOS backend is optimized for **Apple Silicon (M1 or newer)** and uses **Metal** GPU acceleration. *(macOS Intel hardware is completely unsupported)*.
3. **Add Models:** Drop your weights into `app/models/` or download them via the **Model Manager** tab.
4. **Generate:** Open `http://localhost:1420` in your browser.

### Windows

| GPU Vendor | Tech | Status | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nvidia** | CUDA | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-cuda.exe` with Nvidia SDK 12 optimizations. |
| **AMD Radeon** | Vulkan | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-vulkan.exe` with Vulkan API acceleration. |
| **Intel Arc** | Vulkan | ✅ Native | Maps `sd-vulkan.exe` for Intel hardware. |
| **Integrated / None** | CPU | ⚠️ Fallback | Runs on logical CPU threads (slow). |

### Linux

| GPU Vendor | Primary | Fallback | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **NVIDIA** | CUDA / Vulkan | Vulkan / CPU | Auto-detects NVIDIA. Prompt-driven CUDA setup downloads prebuilt or compiles from source. Falls back to Vulkan for GTX. |
| **AMD Radeon** | ROCm | Vulkan | ROCm provides best AMD performance when host ROCm drivers are available. |
| **Intel Arc / integrated** | Vulkan | CPU | Cross-vendor Vulkan support. |
| **Intel Core Ultra NPU** | OpenVINO NPU | CPU | Requires the Intel Linux NPU driver, kernel 6.6+, Python 3, and `./linux.sh --setup-openvino`. |
| **Integrated / None** | CPU | — | Runs on logical CPU threads (slow). |

| Hardware | Primary | Fallback | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Apple Silicon (M1 or newer)** | Metal | CPU | Uses the official Darwin arm64 stable-diffusion.cpp backend. |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **System Requirements & Notes:**
> - **64-bit Windows 10 or Windows 11** is required for the portable Node.js 22 runtime used by the Windows launcher.
> - **glibc 2.38 or newer** is required for the prebuilt Linux backends (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40+, etc.). The setup script will warn you if your glibc is older.
> - **Linux runtime libraries:** The prebuilt backends require `libgomp.so.1`; Vulkan additionally requires `libvulkan.so.1` and a working GPU driver. The setup script now checks these before installing a backend and prints the exact distro package command when one is missing.
> - **Linux OpenVINO NPU:** Intel Core Ultra, x86_64 Linux, kernel 6.6+, a working `/dev/accel/accel0` device, Python 3 with `venv`, and the Intel Linux NPU driver are required.

## <a id="troubleshooting-faq"></a>🛠️ Troubleshooting & FAQ

<details>
  <summary><strong> Reset Environment: If a build fails or you want to clear dependencies</strong></summary>
  <p>Run <code>scripts/reset/reset.ps1</code> (Windows) or <code>scripts/reset/reset.sh</code> (Linux/macOS). This will clear temporary compilation and package caches to repair your environment. <em>(Note: This preserves your model weights and generated output images).</em></p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux backends fail to start with <code>GLIBC_2.38 not found</code></strong></summary>
  <p>The prebuilt binaries require glibc 2.38+ (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04). If your distribution uses an older glibc version, you can upgrade your operating system or compile the backend from source (see the <a href="#building-from-source">Building From Source</a> guide below).</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Port Conflicts: Default port address already busy</strong></summary>
  <p>The web user interface runs on port <code>1420</code> by default. The GPU backend manager attempts to bind to port <code>8080</code> first, then automatically detects and falls back to a free system port if <code>8080</code> is already occupied.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Opening the studio from another device on your network</strong></summary>
  <p>The web interface only accepts connections from the computer it runs on, because it has no login. To reach it from another device on purpose, start it with <code>UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0</code> (for example <code>UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0 ./linux.sh</code>, or <code>set UAIS_HOST=0.0.0.0</code> before running <code>windows.bat</code>). Anyone on that network can then use it.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux ROCm not loading for AMD Radeon GPUs</strong></summary>
  <p>Ensure your AMD GPU hardware and host kernel are fully compatible with ROCm 7.13. If ROCm fails to initialize correctly, the application will automatically fall back to Vulkan acceleration.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Linux uses the integrated GPU instead of the discrete GPU</strong></summary>
  <p>On dual-GPU Linux systems, Vulkan device order can put the integrated Intel GPU at <code>vulkan0</code> and the discrete AMD/NVIDIA GPU at <code>vulkan1</code>. The launcher now tries to prefer a discrete Vulkan device when <code>vulkaninfo --summary</code> is available. To force a device manually, start the app with <code>SD_VULKAN_DEVICE=vulkan1 ./linux.sh</code> or use another index such as <code>vulkan0</code>/<code>vulkan2</code>.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Windows exits with code <code>3221225781</code> (0xC0000135)</strong></summary>
  <p>This code means Windows could not locate a required backend DLL:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>For AMD/Intel Vulkan:</strong> Rerun <code>scripts/setup/setup.ps1</code>. Setup installs the required Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime and replaces stale Vulkan binaries with the compatible pinned build. Approve the Windows administrator prompt when it appears.</li>
    <li><strong>For NVIDIA CUDA:</strong> Install or update your NVIDIA graphics driver, then rerun the setup script to restore the CUDA runtime DLLs.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>If setup cannot install the runtime, install Microsoft's official <a href="https://aka.ms/vc14/vc_redist.x64.exe">Visual C++ Redistributable for x64</a> manually, restart Windows, and rerun setup. A custom Vulkan build is not the first fix for this exit code.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Windows exits with code <code>3221225501</code> (0xC000001D)</strong></summary>
  <p>This is an illegal CPU instruction from an older machine-specific Windows backend build; it is not evidence that the model or RTX GPU is unsupported. Rerun <code>scripts/setup/setup.ps1</code> to replace the CPU/CUDA binaries with runtime-dispatched builds and install the matching CUDA 12.8 runtime. The corrected CUDA package includes Blackwell targets for RTX 50-series GPUs.</p>
</details>

<details>
  <summary><strong> Generation shows "server is not responding or crashed"</strong></summary>
  <p>This indicates that the local backend engine process terminated. Check your launch terminal (where you executed <code>windows.bat</code>, <code>./linux.sh</code>, or <code>./mac.sh</code>) for the exact console error. Common causes include glibc version mismatches, missing Vulkan drivers, or system out-of-memory (OOM) issues.</p>
</details>
